sanskrit: putrāṃś ciragatāñ jñātvā sagaro raghunandana naptāram abravīd rājā dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā
english: Knowing that his sons had been gone a long time, O delight of the Raghu line, king Sagara addressed his grandson, who blazed with his own brilliance.

sanskrit: śūraś ca kṛtavidyaś ca pūrvais tulyo 'si tejasā pitṝṇāṃ gatim anviccha yena cāśvo 'pahāritaḥ
english: "You are both a hero and a man of learning, equal in splendour to your forebears. Search out the fate of your fathers and find the one by whom the sacrificial horse was stolen."

sanskrit: antarbhaumāni sattvāni vīryavanti mahānti ca teṣāṃ tvaṃ pratighātārthaṃ sāsiṃ gṛhṇīṣva kārmukam
english: "There are mighty and powerful creatures dwelling underground. To counter them, take up your sword and bow."

sanskrit: abhivādyābhivādyāṃs tvaṃ hatvā vighnakarān api siddhārthaḥ saṃnivartasva mama yajñasya pāragaḥ
english: "Pay homage to those worthy of homage, but also slay the obstructors. Return with your purpose accomplished, having brought my sacrifice to completion."

sanskrit: evam ukto 'ṃśumān samyak sagareṇa mahātmanā dhanur ādāya khaḍgaṃ ca jagāma laghuvikramaḥ
english: Thus properly addressed by the great-souled Sagara, Aṃśumān took up his bow and sword and set forth with swift strides.

sanskrit: sa khātaṃ pitṛbhir mārgam antarbhaumaṃ mahātmabhiḥ prāpadyata naraśreṣṭha tena rājñābhicoditaḥ
english: Urged on by the king, O best of men, he entered the underground passage that had been dug by those great-souled fathers.

sanskrit: daityadānavarakṣobhiḥ piśācapatagoragaiḥ pūjyamānaṃ mahātejā diśāgajam apaśyata
english: The greatly radiant one beheld the elephant of the quarter, worshipped by Daityas, Dānavas, Rākṣasas, Piśācas, birds, and serpents.

sanskrit: sa taṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā pṛṣṭvā caiva nirāmayam pitṝn sa paripapraccha vājihartāram eva ca
english: He circumambulated it reverently, inquired of its well-being, and then asked after his fathers and the one who had stolen the horse.

sanskrit: diśāgajas tu tac chrutvā prītyāhāṃśumato vacaḥ āsamañjakṛtārthas tvaṃ sahāśvaḥ śīghram eṣyasi
english: The elephant of the quarter, hearing his words, replied to Aṃśumān with gladness: "You will soon return together with the horse, having fulfilled the purpose of Asamañja."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā sarvān eva diśāgajān yathākramaṃ yathānyāyaṃ praṣṭuṃ samupacakrame
english: Hearing those words, he proceeded in due order, according to proper custom, to question all the elephants of the quarters.

sanskrit: taiś ca sarvair diśāpālair vākyajñair vākyakovidaiḥ pūjitaḥ sahayaś caiva gantāsīty abhicoditaḥ
english: Honoured by all those guardians of the quarters, skilled in speech and expert in discourse, he was assured: "You will depart with the horse."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā jagāma laghuvikramaḥ bhasmarāśīkṛtā yatra pitaras tasya sāgarāḥ
english: Hearing their words, swift-striding Aṃśumān went to the place where his paternal uncles, the sons of Sagara, had been reduced to heaps of ash.

sanskrit: sa duḥkhavaśam āpannas tv asamañjasutas tadā cukrośa paramārtas tu vadhāt teṣāṃ suduḥkhitaḥ
english: Overcome with grief, the son of Asamañja cried out in utter anguish, deeply distressed at their destruction.

sanskrit: yajñiyaṃ ca hayaṃ tatra carantam avidūrataḥ dadarśa puruṣavyāghro duḥkhaśokasamanvitaḥ
english: That tiger among men, filled with grief and sorrow, also saw the sacrificial horse wandering not far away.

sanskrit: dadarśa puruṣavyāghro kartukāmo jalakriyām salilārthī mahātejā na cāpaśyaj jalāśayam
english: That tiger among men, the greatly radiant one, wishing to perform the water-oblation for them, sought water but found no body of water nearby.

sanskrit: visārya nipuṇāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ tato 'paśyat khagādhipam pitṝṇāṃ mātulaṃ rāma suparṇam anilopamam
english: Casting his gaze carefully in all directions, O Rāma, he then saw Suparṇa — Garuḍa, the lord of birds, the maternal uncle of his forefathers — matchless and without blemish.

sanskrit: sa cainam abravīd vākyaṃ vainateyo mahābalaḥ mā śucaḥ puruṣavyāghra vadho 'yaṃ lokasaṃmataḥ
english: The mighty Vainateya, Garuḍa, spoke these words to him: "Do not grieve, O tiger among men. This slaying was sanctioned by the world."

sanskrit: kapilenāprameyena dagdhā hīme mahābalāḥ salilaṃ nārhasi prājña dātum eṣāṃ hi laukikam
english: "These mighty ones were burned by the immeasurable Kapila. You should not, O wise one, offer them ordinary water — that mundane rite is not appropriate for them."

sanskrit: gaṅgā himavato jyeṣṭhā duhitā puruṣarṣabha bhasmarāśīkṛtān etān pāvayel lokapāvanī
english: "Gaṅgā, the elder daughter of Himavat, O bull among men — she who purifies all worlds — can sanctify these who have been reduced to heaps of ash."

sanskrit: tayā klinnam idaṃ bhasma gaṅgayā lokakāntayā ṣaṣṭiṃ putrasahasrāṇi svargalokaṃ nayiṣyati
english: "When this ash is moistened by Gaṅgā, the beloved of all worlds, she will carry those sixty thousand sons to the heavenly realm."

sanskrit: gaccha cāśvaṃ mahābhāga saṃgṛhya puruṣarṣabha yajñaṃ paitāmahaṃ vīra nirvartayitum arhasi
english: "Go now, O greatly fortunate bull among men, take the horse, and complete your grandfather's sacrifice — that is what you must do, O hero."

sanskrit: suparṇavacanaṃ śrutvā so 'ṃśumān ativīryavān tvaritaṃ hayam ādāya punar āyān mahāyaśāḥ
english: Hearing Suparṇa's words, the exceedingly valiant and greatly glorious Aṃśumān swiftly took the horse and returned.

sanskrit: tato rājānam āsādya dīkṣitaṃ raghunandana nyavedayad yathāvṛttaṃ suparṇavacanaṃ tathā
english: Then, reaching the king who was consecrated for the sacrifice, O delight of the Raghu line, he reported in full what had happened and likewise Suparṇa's words.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā ghorasaṃkāśaṃ vākyam aṃśumato nṛpaḥ yajñaṃ nirvartayām āsa yathākalpaṃ yathāvidhi
english: Hearing those dreadful tidings from Aṃśumān, the king completed the sacrifice in full accordance with ritual injunction and prescribed rule.

sanskrit: svapuraṃ cāgamac chrīmān iṣṭayajño mahīpatiḥ gaṅgāyāś cāgame rājā niścayaṃ nādhyagacchata
english: The glorious king of the earth, having completed his desired sacrifice, returned to his own city, yet the king could not arrive at any resolution concerning the bringing of Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: agatvā niścayaṃ rājā kālena mahatā mahān triṃśadvarṣasahasrāṇi rājyaṃ kṛtvā divaṃ gataḥ
english: Without reaching a resolution, the great king, after a long passage of time — thirty thousand years of ruling — ascended to heaven.

sanskrit: kāladharmaṃ gate rāma sagare prakṛtījanāḥ rājānaṃ rocayām āsur aṃśumantaṃ sudhārmikam
english: When Sagara had gone the way of time, O Rāma, the subjects acclaimed the greatly righteous Aṃśumān as king.

sanskrit: sa rājā sumahān āsīd aṃśumān raghunandana tasya putro mahān āsīd dilīpa iti viśrutaḥ
english: That great king Aṃśumān reigned magnificently, O delight of the Raghu line, and his great son was known as Dilīpa.

sanskrit: tasmin rājyaṃ samāveśya dilīpe raghunandana himavacchikhare ramye tapas tepe sudāruṇam
english: Entrusting the kingdom to Dilīpa, O delight of the Raghu line, he performed extremely severe austerities on a beautiful peak of Himavat.

sanskrit: dvātriṃśac ca sahasrāṇi varṣāṇi sumahāyaśāḥ tapovanagato rājā svargaṃ lebhe tapodhanaḥ
english: For thirty-two thousand years that greatly glorious king, dwelling in the austerity-grove and rich in the wealth of penance, won heaven.

sanskrit: dilīpas tu mahātejāḥ śrutvā paitāmahaṃ vadham duḥkhopahatayā buddhyā niścayaṃ nādhyagacchata
english: But Dilīpa of great splendour, upon hearing of his great-grandfathers' destruction, could arrive at no resolution, his mind afflicted with grief.

sanskrit: kathaṃ gaṅgāvataraṇaṃ kathaṃ teṣāṃ jalakriyā tārayeyaṃ kathaṃ caitān iti cintā paro 'bhavat
english: "How is Gaṅgā to descend? How are the water-rites for them to be performed? How can I liberate these ancestors?" — thus was he wholly absorbed in anxiety.

sanskrit: tasya cintayato nityaṃ dharmeṇa viditātmanaḥ putro bhagīratho nāma jajñe paramadhārmikaḥ
english: While he was constantly pondering thus — he who had known the self through righteousness — a son was born to him named Bhagīratha, supremely virtuous.

sanskrit: dilīpas tu mahātejā yajñair bahubhir iṣṭavān triṃśadvarṣasahasrāṇi rājā rājyam akārayat
english: Dilīpa of great splendour, having performed many sacrifices and worshipped the gods, ruled his kingdom for thirty thousand years.

sanskrit: agatvā niścayaṃ rājā teṣām uddharaṇaṃ prati vyādhinā naraśārdūla kāladharmam upeyivān
english: Without reaching a resolution concerning the rescue of those ancestors, the king, O tiger among men, succumbed to illness and met the law of time.

sanskrit: indralokaṃ gato rājā svārjitenaiva karmaṇā rājye bhagīrathaṃ putram abhiṣicya nararṣabhaḥ
english: That bull among men, the king, having anointed his son Bhagīratha on the throne, went to Indra's realm by virtue of his own accumulated merit.

sanskrit: bhagīrathas tu rājarṣir dhārmiko raghunandana anapatyo mahātejāḥ prajākāmaḥ sa cāprajaḥ
english: Bhagīratha, the royal sage, righteous and of great splendour, O delight of the Raghu line, was childless; though he longed for offspring, he had none.

sanskrit: sa tapo dīrgham ātiṣṭhad gokarṇe raghunandana ūrdhvabāhuḥ pañcatapā māsāhāro jitendriyaḥ
english: He undertook prolonged austerities at Gokarṇa, O delight of the Raghu line — arms raised, surrounded by five fires, eating only once a month, his senses fully subdued.

sanskrit: tasya varṣasahasrāṇi ghore tapasi tiṣṭhataḥ suprīto bhagavān brahmā prajānāṃ patir īśvaraḥ
english: As he continued in that fierce austerity for thousands of years, the blessed Brahmā, the lord and master of all creatures, was greatly pleased.

sanskrit: tataḥ suragaṇaiḥ sārdham upāgamya pitāmahaḥ bhagīrathaṃ mahātmānaṃ tapyamānam athābravīt
english: Then the Grandfather, approaching together with the hosts of gods, spoke thus to the great-souled Bhagīratha who was practising his austerities.

sanskrit: bhagīratha mahābhāga prītas te 'haṃ janeśvara tapasā ca sutaptena varaṃ varaya suvrata
english: "O greatly fortunate Bhagīratha, lord of the people, I am pleased with you and with your intensely performed austerities. Choose a boon, O man of excellent vows."

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahātejāḥ sarvalokapitāmaham bhagīratho mahābhāgaḥ kṛtāñjalir avasthitaḥ
english: The greatly splendid and greatly fortunate Bhagīratha, standing with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus to him, the grandfather of all worlds.

sanskrit: yadi me bhagavān prīto yady asti tapasaḥ phalam sagarasyātmajāḥ sarve mattaḥ salilam āpnuyuḥ
english: "If you, O blessed one, are pleased with me, and if my austerities have borne fruit, then may all the sons of Sagara receive water-oblations from my hand."

sanskrit: gaṅgāyāḥ salilaklinne bhasmany eṣāṃ mahātmanām svargaṃ gaccheyur atyantaṃ sarve me prapitāmahāḥ
english: "May the ashes of these great-souled ones be moistened by the waters of Gaṅgā, and may all of my great-grandfathers thereby attain the highest heaven."

sanskrit: deyā ca saṃtatir deva nāvasīdet kulaṃ ca naḥ ikṣvākūṇāṃ kule deva eṣa me 'stu varaḥ paraḥ
english: "And may offspring be granted, O god, so that our lineage does not perish — let the line of the Ikṣvākus not decline, O god. Let this be the paramount boon for me."

sanskrit: uktavākyaṃ tu rājānaṃ sarvalokapitāmahaḥ pratyuvāca śubhāṃ vāṇīṃ madhurāṃ madhurākṣarām
english: To the king who had thus spoken, the grandfather of all worlds replied with a gentle, sweet speech, sweet in every syllable.

sanskrit: manoratho mahān eṣa bhagīratha mahāratha evaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ te ikṣvākukulavardhana
english: "This is a great desire of the heart, O Bhagīratha, great chariot-warrior. Let it be so. May it be auspicious for you, O increaser of the Ikṣvāku line."

sanskrit: iyaṃ haimavatī gaṅgā jyeṣṭhā himavataḥ sutā tāṃ vai dhārayituṃ rājan haras tatra niyujyatām
english: "This Gaṅgā, daughter of Himavat, born of the snows, the eldest daughter of Himavat — in order to bear her descent, O king, Hara must be engaged for that purpose."

sanskrit: gaṅgāyāḥ patanaṃ rājan pṛthivī na sahiṣyate tāṃ vai dhārayituṃ vīra nānyaṃ paśyāmi śūlinaḥ
english: "The earth will not be able to bear Gaṅgā's fall, O king. To bear her, O hero, I see no one other than the wielder of the trident, Śūlin — Śiva."

sanskrit: tam evam uktvā rājānaṃ gaṅgāṃ cābhāṣya lokakṛt jagāma tridivaṃ devaḥ saha sarvair marudgaṇaiḥ
english: Having spoken thus to the king, and having addressed Gaṅgā as well, the creator of worlds, the god, departed to the three heavens together with all the hosts of Maruts.

sanskrit: devadeve gate tasmin so 'ṅguṣṭhāgranipīḍitām kṛtvā vasumatīṃ rāma saṃvatsaram upāsata
english: When that god of gods had departed, O Rāma, Bhagīratha stood on the tip of his big toe pressing the earth, and in that posture he worshipped for a full year.

sanskrit: atha saṃvatsare pūrṇe sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ umāpatiḥ paśupatī rājānam idam abravīt
english: Then, when the year was complete, Umāpati, Paśupati, the lord saluted by all worlds, spoke these words to the king.

sanskrit: prītas te 'haṃ naraśreṣṭha kariṣyāmi tava priyam śirasā dhārayiṣyāmi śailarājasutām aham
english: "I am pleased with you, O best of men, and I will do what is dear to you. I will bear upon my head the daughter of the mountain-king."

sanskrit: tato haimavatī jyeṣṭhā sarvalokanamaskṛtā tadā sātimahad rūpaṃ kṛtvā vegaṃ ca duḥsaham ākāśād apatad rāma śive śivaśirasy uta
english: Then the eldest daughter of the snowy mountain, saluted by all the worlds, assumed a form of immense size and unbearable velocity, and fell from the sky, O Rāma — fell indeed upon the auspicious head of the auspicious Śiva.

sanskrit: naiva sā nirgamaṃ lebhe jaṭāmaṇḍalamohitā tatraivābabhramad devī saṃvatsaragaṇān bahūn
english: She found no way out, bewildered within the tangle of matted locks, and the goddess wandered there for many years.

sanskrit: anena toṣitaś cāsīd atyarthaṃ raghunandana visasarja tato gaṅgāṃ haro bindusaraḥ prati
english: Bhagīratha had greatly pleased Hara by this act, O delight of the Raghu line, and so Hara released Gaṅgā in the direction of Bindu Lake.

sanskrit: gaganāc chaṃkaraśiras tato dharaṇim āgatā vyasarpata jalaṃ tatra tīvraśabdapuraskṛtam
english: From Śaṃkara's head, descending from the sky to the earth, the water spread out there, preceded by a tremendous roar.

sanskrit: tato devarṣigandharvā yakṣāḥ siddhagaṇās tathā vyalokayanta te tatra gaganād gāṃ gatāṃ tadā
english: Then gods, sages, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, and hosts of Siddhas all gazed upon her as she passed from the sky down to the earth.

sanskrit: vimānair nagarākārair hayair gajavarais tathā pāriplavagatāś cāpi devatās tatra viṣṭhitāḥ
english: The divinities were stationed there in aerial chariots shaped like cities, on horses and on magnificent elephants, and some hovered aloft, darting to and fro.

sanskrit: tad adbhutatamaṃ loke gaṅgāpatanam uttamam didṛkṣavo devagaṇāḥ sameyur amitaujasaḥ
english: That most wonderful and supreme descent of Gaṅgā — the assembled hosts of gods of immeasurable might gathered to behold it.

sanskrit: saṃpatadbhiḥ suragaṇais teṣāṃ cābharaṇaujasā śatādityam ivābhāti gaganaṃ gatatoyadam
english: With the hosts of gods rushing through it and the lustre of their ornaments blazing, the sky — drained of its clouds — shone as if lit by a hundred suns.

sanskrit: śiṃśumāroragagaṇair mīnair api ca cañcalaiḥ vidyudbhir iva vikṣiptair ākāśam abhavat tadā
english: With Śiṃśumāra sea-creatures, hosts of serpents, and flashing fish darting about like scattered bolts of lightning, the sky blazed brilliantly at that moment.

sanskrit: pāṇḍuraiḥ salilotpīḍaiḥ kīryamāṇaiḥ sahasradhā śāradābhrair ivākīrṇaṃ gaganaṃ haṃsasaṃplavaiḥ
english: With white surging sprays of water scattered in a thousand streams, the sky was covered as if with autumn clouds, or as if carpeted by flocks of swans in flight.

sanskrit: kva cid drutataraṃ yāti kuṭilaṃ kva cid āyatam vinataṃ kva cid uddhūtaṃ kva cid yāti śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
english: Somewhere she rushed very swiftly; somewhere she wound in curves; somewhere she stretched out long; somewhere she dipped low; somewhere she was tossed up high; somewhere she moved very slowly.

sanskrit: salilenaiva salilaṃ kva cid abhyāhataṃ punaḥ muhur ūrdhvapathaṃ gatvā papāta vasudhāṃ punaḥ
english: Somewhere water struck water and bounced back; repeatedly going upward and then falling again to the earth.

sanskrit: tac chaṃkaraśirobhraṣṭaṃ bhraṣṭaṃ bhūmitale punaḥ vyarocata tadā toyaṃ nirmalaṃ gatakalmaṣam
english: That water, having fallen from Śaṃkara's head, and then having fallen to the surface of the earth, then shone brilliantly — pure, its impurities gone.

sanskrit: tatrarṣigaṇagandharvā vasudhātalavāsinaḥ bhavāṅgapatitaṃ toyaṃ pavitram iti paspṛśuḥ
english: There the hosts of sages and Gandharvas dwelling on the surface of the earth touched that water which had fallen from the body of Bhava — Śiva — knowing it to be holy.

sanskrit: śāpāt prapatitā ye ca gaganād vasudhātalam kṛtvā tatrābhiṣekaṃ te babhūvur gatakalmaṣāḥ
english: Those who had fallen from the sky to the surface of the earth through a curse — bathing in those waters, they became free of all impurity.

sanskrit: dhūpapāpāḥ punas tena toyenātha subhāsvatā punar ākāśam āviśya svāṃl lokān pratipedire
english: Their sins washed away and purified by those brilliantly shining waters, they re-entered the sky and regained their own celestial realms.

sanskrit: mumude mudito lokas tena toyena bhāsvatā kṛtābhiṣeko gaṅgāyāṃ babhūva vigataklamaḥ
english: The world rejoiced, rejoiced in those shining waters; whoever bathed in Gaṅgā became free from fatigue and weariness.

sanskrit: bhagīratho 'pi rājarṣir divyaṃ syandanam āsthitaḥ prāyād agre mahātejās taṃ gaṅgā pṛṣṭhato 'nvagāt
english: And the royal sage Bhagīratha, of great splendour, mounted his divine chariot and drove forward, while Gaṅgā followed behind him.

sanskrit: devāḥ sarṣigaṇāḥ sarve daityadānavarākṣasāḥ gandharvayakṣapravarāḥ sakiṃnaramahoragāḥ
english: All the gods together with their hosts of sages, Daityas, Dānavas, Rākṣasas, the foremost of Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Kiṃnaras, and the great serpents —

sanskrit: sarvāś cāpsaraso rāma bhagīratharathānugāḥ gaṅgām anvagaman prītāḥ sarve jalacarāś ca ye
english: — and all the Apsarasas, O Rāma, following in the wake of Bhagīratha's chariot, joyfully followed Gaṅgā, as did all the creatures that live in water.

sanskrit: yato bhagīratho rājā tato gaṅgā yaśasvinī jagāma saritāṃ śreṣṭhā sarvapāpavināśinī
english: Wherever king Bhagīratha went, thither went the glorious Gaṅgā, the best of rivers, the destroyer of all sins.
